title: The CLI alone carries the guidance (no agent, no skill installed)
expectation: An agent holding only the binary, with no skill installed and no network, must be able to reach the guidance from the CLI itself: `monochange --help` advertises the skill surface, `monochange skill` lists the bundled topics, `monochange skill read <topic>` serves the document verbatim as raw Markdown, `monochange skill install --dir` writes a usable tree and refuses to clobber an existing one, and an unknown topic exits non-zero. These are deterministic properties, so they are pinned here rather than graded from a stochastic agent run.

checks.why: Discovery starts at `monochange --help`, the first thing the skill tells an agent to inspect.
The listing is the index an agent scans before choosing what to read, and it must advertise both actions.
The entrypoint must carry the routing and the guardrails, byte for byte as published.
These are the facts the evaluations showed agents need: how to declare packages, and how versioned files and dependency prefixes are configured.
The changeset file shape and the propagation escape hatch are the two things an agent must get right when recording release intent.
Agents parse the document itself, so terminal rendering would corrupt frontmatter and code blocks.

checks.command: rm -rf .work-bytes && monochange skill install --dir .work-bytes/monochange >/dev/null && monochange skill read configuration > .work-config.md && cmp -s .work-config.md .work-bytes/monochange/skills/configuration.md
checks.why: An agent that reads a topic and an agent that installs the skill must receive the same document; otherwise one channel silently serves different guidance.

checks.command: rm -rf .work-install && monochange skill install --dir .work-install/monochange && test -f .work-install/monochange/SKILL.md && test -f .work-install/monochange/skills/configuration.md && head -1 .work-install/monochange/SKILL.md | grep -qx -- '---'
checks.why: An install must produce the whole skill tree with the entrypoint intact, not just the entrypoint.
Replacing a curated skill is not a side effect an install may have without --force.
The explicit override must exist and work, and the run workdir must be left clean.
A scripting agent relies on exit status, not prose, to notice a misspelled topic.
